question: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
solution:
The correct answer is __**four times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is mathematically expressed by the formula: **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the body and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• From the formula, it is evident that the **kinetic energy** of a body is **directly proportional** to the **square of its velocity** (KE ∝ v²), assuming the **mass** remains constant.
 
• If the **velocity** of a body is **doubled** (v becomes 2v), the new kinetic energy (KE') can be calculated as: **KE' = 1/2 m(2v)² = 1/2 m(4v²) = 4 (1/2 mv²)**.
 
• Therefore, when the velocity is increased by a **factor of 2**, the kinetic energy increases by a factor of **2 squared**, which is **4**. Hence, the kinetic energy becomes **four times** its original value.
 
• This relationship highlights that **kinetic energy** is highly sensitive to changes in **speed** compared to changes in **mass**. For instance, if the velocity were tripled, the kinetic energy would become **nine times** the original.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. If **positive work** is done on a body, its **velocity** increases, leading to a rise in kinetic energy.
 
• **Relationship with Momentum**: Kinetic energy is also related to **linear momentum (p)** by the formula **KE = p² / 2m**. This shows that if the **momentum** of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy also becomes **four times**, provided the **mass** is constant.
 
• **Units and Nature**: The **SI unit** of kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 kg m²/s²**. Kinetic energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only **magnitude** and no **direction**, and it can never be **negative** because mass is positive and the square of velocity is always non-negative.
 
• **Practical Applications**: This principle is critical in **road safety**. Since **KE ∝ v²**, doubling the speed of a car quadruples the energy involved in a **collision** and significantly increases the **braking distance** required to stop the vehicle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass vs. Velocity**: While kinetic energy is **linearly proportional** to **mass**, it is **quadratically proportional** to **velocity**. Doubling the **mass** only doubles the kinetic energy, but doubling the **velocity** quadruples it.
 
• **Frame of Reference**: The value of kinetic energy depends on the **observer's frame of reference**. A person sitting in a moving train has **zero kinetic energy** relative to the train but significant kinetic energy relative to an observer standing on the **platform**.
 
• **Types of Kinetic Energy**: Besides **translational kinetic energy** (1/2 mv²), objects can also possess **rotational kinetic energy** (1/2 Iω²) and **vibrational kinetic energy**, depending on their type of motion.
